story.so_that: I can add new workflows by creating a package and registering it in the orchestrator catalog without modifying existing workflow code or entangling generic infrastructure with domain behavior
story.i_want: to refactor the orchestrator package into three layers (common, orchestrator, and workflow modules) with a stable module contract

related_acceptance_criteria.criterion: common contains generic interfaces and infrastructure and imports no workflow package or orchestrator module
related_acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given the common package is created When its imports are analyzed Then it contains no references to orchestrator or any workflow package

related_acceptance_criteria.criterion: each workflow package imports generic capabilities from common and never imports another workflow package
related_acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a workflow package exists When its imports are analyzed Then it imports only common and its own modules

related_acceptance_criteria.criterion: orchestrator contains no Story Analysis skill names, grading rules, artifact conventions, Activity implementations, or result details
related_acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given the orchestrator package is refactored When its source is searched for Story Analysis domain concepts Then no skill names, grading rules, artifact conventions, Activity implementations, or result details remain

related_acceptance_criteria.criterion: a second workflow is mounted by adding its package and orchestrator catalog entry, without changing Story Analysis code
related_acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a new workflow package exists When it is added to the orchestrator catalog Then Story Analysis code is unchanged and the new workflow runs independently

related_acceptance_criteria.criterion: all common, workflow-module, orchestrator, and live Cadence integration tests pass
related_acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given the refactor is complete When the test suites and integration tests run Then all common, workflow-module, orchestrator, and live Cadence tests pass

related_acceptance_criteria.criterion: a second workflow is mounted and both it and Story Analysis run on independent Workers without code changes
related_acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a second workflow package and catalog entry exist When the orchestrator starts and a representative workflow run is started Then both Workers poll and the new workflow executes without modifying Story Analysis files

related_acceptance_criteria.criterion: workflow module dependency violations are detected and rejected
related_acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a workflow module descriptor or source imports another workflow package or the orchestrator When it is loaded Then validation or static checks fail the module

related_edge_cases.criterion: Duplicate module names or duplicate workflow/Activity wire names
related_edge_cases.gherkin: Given the catalog contains two modules with the same name or overlapping wire names within a Worker registry When the orchestrator composes the registry Then it detects the conflict and fails startup

related_edge_cases.criterion: Two modules configured for the same domain and task list
related_edge_cases.gherkin: Given two modules declare the same domain and task list When the orchestrator groups them Then they share one Worker if names do not conflict, or fail if they do
Given the Cadence server is not reachable When the orchestrator creates a Worker Then startup fails with a clear domain or client error

related_edge_cases.criterion: Partial Worker failure in a multi-Worker process
related_edge_cases.gherkin: Given one of several Workers fails to start or crashes When the orchestrator is running Then it cancels remaining Workers and reports the failure

related_edge_cases.criterion: Single-Activity diagnostic workflow without resolved task-list routing
related_edge_cases.gherkin: Given the diagnostic workflow is started and no routing design has been chosen When it executes Then it does not silently schedule on the wrong task list and the open behavior is documented

related_edge_cases.criterion: Workflow module that imports another workflow package or orchestrator
related_edge_cases.gherkin: Given a workflow module source or descriptor imports a disallowed package When dependency checks run Then the violation is caught before the module is mounted

steps.description: Add Cadence SDK characterization tests for registry.workflow(name=...)(WorkflowClass), Activity registration, and Worker async context entry and exit
Add static architecture tests enforcing common <- workflow modules <- orchestrator and rejecting Story Analysis domain concepts in orchestrator
Add unit suites for descriptor validation, catalog errors and empty behavior, grouping and conflicts, declaration-registration consistency, diagnostics, and AsyncExitStack rollback
Create a minimal second workflow fixture and catalog override on a distinct domain and task list
Run integration tests proving unchanged Story Analysis behavior, two independent Workers, route-scoped diagnostics, and cleanup after a later Worker startup failure
Run end-to-end script scenarios for normal multi-Worker startup and stop, an empty catalog, and an invalid module path
Run all unit, integration, and E2E suites and verify stale Story Analysis implementations and imports have been removed from orchestrator
